why: The vocabulary a claim may declare, read from the module that enforces it
narration: Every claim this project draws carries one word from this list. There are @n.truth.classes of them. What is on screen is not a summary. It is that line of the module that enforces it, with the file, the line number, and the digest of those bytes.

why: Not injective — a material cannot be read backwards (the module's own heading)
narration: @n.truth.classes classes, @n.truth.materials materials. There are fewer materials than classes, so a surface cannot be read backwards to the class behind it. And the last clause is on screen with the rest: anything unreadable falls to fog, never to a default.

why: The verdict words a row may carry, and the description that ships beside them
narration: @n.truth.verdict_words words, and no percentage anywhere in the schema. A score can be averaged until a failure disappears into it. These cannot. The description on screen defines the least comfortable of them: a claim withdrawn, and a gate registered but never run.

asks: Can a check exit zero without printing the word PASS?
source: viewer/gate_runner.cjs — the law: exit zero if and only if the printed verdict is PASS
note: In the canonical ledger: @n.gap.in_ledger of @n.gap.registered registered gates.
narration: The law here is narrow. A check may exit zero only if it also printed the word PASS, and the runner asserts that over every gate it ran. The line at the foot asks a different question of the same registry. Its answer is there too.

asks: Does every concept in the registry point at a line that exists?
source: viewer/verify_concepts.cjs --mutate — the registry is broken on purpose and the check must notice
narration: Every concept in this registry names a file and a line. This check opens each one. It ran with its mutation suite, which breaks the registry on purpose and requires the check to notice. What it cannot settle is whether an anchor is the right anchor.

asks: Does an evidence pack survive a round trip, and is a forged one caught?
source: viewer/verify_bag.cjs --mutate — every mutation is required to FAIL verification
note: Independent custodians: @n.witness.independent_custodians — claim level tamper_evident, never authenticated.
narration: This packs the evidence, ships it, unpacks it, then forges it on purpose to see whether the forgery is refused. The note under the frame names what that is worth. Tamper-evident, and not unforgeable. The count of independent custodians is beside it.
